notes.common/climate-correlation-networks.md:
# Climate correlation networks

Network-theory and complexity-science approaches that treat dynamical coupling within the tropical Pacific and with remote oceans as precursors of [ENSO](enso.md) evolution, enabling forecasts beyond the seasonal timescale. [network/complexity · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

In this paper the route is **background positioning** (citations [23, 24]), not the implemented algorithm; keep it separate from [XRO](extended-recharge-oscillator.md), [deep learning](deep-learning.md), and [hybrid](physics-guided-hybrid-enso-forecasting.md) methods.

Related Library preprint ([paper hub](../paper-f2e5cb4961564e52/index.md)): *Climate network and complexity based ENSO forecast for 2026* (`paper-f2e5cb4961564e52`).

notes.common/deep-learning.md:
# Deep Learning

Data-driven neural architectures that extract spatiotemporal patterns from high-dimensional climate fields. For [ENSO](enso.md), the Introduction cites convolutional landmark models and transformer-style systems such as 3D-Geoformer that can push Niño3.4 skill beyond ~18 months, at high compute cost and with limited physical interpretability. [DL for ENSO · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

Distinct from the [XRO](extended-recharge-oscillator.md) physical route and from [physics-guided hybrids](physics-guided-hybrid-enso-forecasting.md) that constrain ML with conceptual modes.

# El Niño–Southern Oscillation

Dominant mode of interannual climate variability arising from nonlinear ocean–atmosphere coupling in the tropical Pacific, with global impacts on extremes, ecosystems, and society. [ENSO definition · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

Forecasting routes in this Library should stay distinct: physical recharge oscillators / [XRO](extended-recharge-oscillator.md), [climate correlation networks](climate-correlation-networks.md), [deep learning](deep-learning.md), and [physics-guided hybrids](physics-guided-hybrid-enso-forecasting.md).

notes.common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md:
# Extended Recharge Oscillator

Physical conceptual route for [ENSO](enso.md): the classical Recharge Oscillator couples SST and equatorial subsurface heat content; the Extended Recharge Oscillator (XRO) embeds ENSO in a multi-basin coupled system and, as cited here, extends predictive skill to roughly 18 months. [RO · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [XRO · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

Keep this route distinct from [deep learning](deep-learning.md), [climate correlation networks](climate-correlation-networks.md), and [physics-guided hybrids](physics-guided-hybrid-enso-forecasting.md) that reuse XRO modes inside ML models.

Primary published source in this Library ([paper hub](../paper-e09bd415cb6849f6/index.md)): Zhao et al., *Explainable El Niño predictability from climate mode interactions* (`paper-e09bd415cb6849f6`).

notes.common/long-lead-enso-predictability.md:
# Long-lead ENSO predictability

The challenge of sustaining skillful [ENSO](enso.md) forecasts beyond seasonal leads, including which couplings set skill and whether an intrinsic predictability horizon exists. [Abstract · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [15–20 month plateau · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

Contemporary physical, deep-learning, and reservoir frameworks often converge near ~15–20 months of skill; error-growth analyses in this paper point toward an intrinsic limit near ~30 months. [~30 months · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

notes.paper-a56c3ee1b33d45b2/index.md:
# Long-term prediction of ENSO with physics-guided Deep Echo State Networks

**Preprint.** arXiv:2601.12251v1 [physics.ao-ph] (18 Jan 2026). [arXiv header · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

## Problem and idea

[ENSO](../common/enso.md) is the leading mode of interannual climate variability, yet the mechanisms that limit **long-lead** forecast skill remain unclear. [Abstract · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [Introduction · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

This paper addresses [long-lead ENSO predictability](../common/long-lead-enso-predictability.md) with a **physics-guided** [hybrid](../common/physics-guided-hybrid-enso-forecasting.md) route: a [Deep Echo State Network (DESN)](physics-guided-desn.md) driven by ten XRO-selected climate modes (including WWV and inter-basin indices) plus seasonal priors, rather than a pure deep network on raw fields. [DESN framework · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [XRO-guided inputs · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

The Introduction situates the work among four Library-relevant ENSO forecasting routes:

1. **Physical recharge oscillators / XRO** — classical [Recharge Oscillator](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md) physics, then the multi-basin [Extended Recharge Oscillator (XRO)](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md) that extends skill toward ~18 months. [RO background · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [XRO · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)
2. **Climate correlation networks** — network/complexity precursors that motivate looking beyond the tropical Pacific alone (cited as background; not the method implemented here). [network theory · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)
3. **Deep learning** — convolutional and transformer models (e.g. 3D-Geoformer) that can exceed ~18-month Niño3.4 skill but are costly and hard to diagnose mechanistically. [DL route · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)
4. **Hybrid / physics-guided ML** — this paper’s answer: guide lightweight reservoir computing with XRO modes to keep skill **and** mechanistic experiments. [central challenge · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [closing framing · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

Library neighbors (no wiki hubs yet; titles only): Zhao et al. 2024 *Explainable El Niño predictability…* (XRO; `paper-e09bd415cb6849f6`); the RO review (`paper-e95322ea3e1f4a2a`); network forecast (`paper-f2e5cb4961564e52`); DL (`paper-db78aff21cda4d55`); dynamical–DL hybrid (`paper-eee57a8421b14218`).

## Key method

[Physics-guided DESN](physics-guided-desn.md) stacks reservoir layers on ORAS5-derived indices (Niño3.4, WWV, NPMM/SPMM, IOB/IOD/SIOD, TNA/ATL3/SASD) plus periodic bootstrap seasonal inputs; only the linear readout is trained (ridge regression), with seconds-scale CPU training. [DESN · p. 20](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [ORAS5 · p. 20](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [efficiency · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

Benchmarks include minimal/full ESN, [XRO](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md), IRI ensembles, and 3D-Geoformer. [baselines · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

## Key results

- **Skill:** Niño3.4 ACC stays above 0.5 out to **16 months** out-of-sample (2002–2023) and up to **20 months** in-sample; abstract summarizes skillful leads of **16–20 months**. [OOS ACC · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [in-sample · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [Abstract · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)
- **Mechanism:** Mode-decoupling/addition experiments show long-lead skill collapses without WWV and emerges only when WWV is coupled to inter-basin modes (NPMM especially); DESN’s advantage over XRO at long leads points to higher-order nonlinearity, supported by SN-XRO. [WWV–cross-basin · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [nonlinearity vs XRO · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [SN-XRO · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)
- **Intrinsic limit:** Absolute-error growth implies predictability horizons ~18 (ESN), ~22 (XRO), ~34 (DESN) months, near an intrinsic ~**30-month** barrier. [error growth · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [~30 months · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

## Limits

Results are reanalysis-based (ORAS5), physics-guided but not causal proofs, and the preprint status should be kept in mind when comparing to peer-reviewed Library papers. [grounded understanding · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5) [preprint · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-026-01360-5)

# Toward long-range ENSO prediction with an explainable deep learning model

**Preprint.** arXiv:2503.19502v1 [physics.geo-ph] (25 Mar 2025). [arXiv header · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)

## Problem and idea

[ENSO](../common/enso.md) forecasting remains limited by nonlinearity, stochasticity, multivariate coupling, and the spring predictability barrier (SPB); traditional statistical/dynamical skill is often cited near ~12 months (correlation > 0.5). [Introduction · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [Abstract · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)

This paper addresses [long-lead ENSO predictability](../common/long-lead-enso-predictability.md) on the **[deep learning](../common/deep-learning.md)** route: it introduces [CTEFNet](ctefnet.md), a multivariate CNN–transformer encoder–decoder that forecasts the Niño 3.4 index from nine ocean–atmosphere fields and adds gradient-based sensitivity analysis for physical precursors. [CTEFNet · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [interpretability · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

Keep Library ENSO routes distinct:

1. **Deep learning (this paper)** — CNNs, transformers, and CNN–transformer hybrids trained on high-dimensional fields; CTEFNet targets multivariate ocean–atmosphere coupling beyond SST-only encoder hybrids. [DL background · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [CTEFNet · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)
2. **Physical recharge oscillators / XRO** — sensitivity findings are interpreted with the classical [recharge-oscillation](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md) and Bjerknes mechanisms (not an XRO forecast model). [recharge oscillation · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [mechanisms · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)
3. **Physics-guided hybrids** — Library neighbor [physics-guided DESN](../paper-a56c3ee1b33d45b2/index.md); do not collapse CTEFNet into that route.
4. **Climate correlation networks** — not the method implemented here.

## Key method

[CTEFNet](ctefnet.md) trains on [CMIP6](../common/cmip6.md) SSP370 ensemble simulations (2015–2100), validates with [ORAS5](../common/oras5.md)/ERA5 (1958–1978), and tests on GODAS/ERA5 (1980–2021). Inputs are 12 months of SST, HC, MLD, SSS, SLP, UO, VO, TAUU, and TAUV; outputs are 24 months of Niño 3.4. [setup · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [data · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [architecture · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)

## Key results

- **Skill:** Effective lead near **20 months** on the [Niño 3.4](../common/nino-3-4-long-lead-forecast.md) task; all-season correlation stays above 0.7 to 12 months and above 0.6 beyond 17 months, beating NMME and several DL baselines (CNN, Geoformer, ResCNN, ResoNet, STPNet) on the reported CMIP6-trained comparison. Seasonal maps keep correlation > 0.5 for >20 months (Jun–Dec) and ~16 months in boreal spring. [Abstract · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [skill · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [seasonality · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)
- **Interpretability:** Gradient sensitivities recover recharge-phase HC/MLD precursors, Bjerknes-like Pacific coupling, and Atlantic/Indian Ocean teleconnection patterns (95% significant grids). [sensitivity · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [early precursors · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [inter-basin · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)

## Limits

Targets Niño 3.4 only (not ENSO diversity/Modoki); SPB is reduced but not removed; preprint status and CMIP6-training/reanalysis-test protocol matter when comparing skill curves across papers. [limits · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w) [preprint · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-025-01159-w)

# Explainable El Niño predictability from climate mode interactions

*Nature* **630**, 891–898 (2024). DOI [10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6). [DOI · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Published online 26 June 2024 · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

## Problem and idea

[ENSO](../common/enso.md) supplies most seasonal climate forecast skill, yet skillful leads beyond one year remain difficult, and the relative roles of remote ocean basins are hard to quantify in biased CGCMs or linear inverse models. [Abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [>1 year challenge · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [basin contributions elusive · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

This paper addresses [long-lead ENSO predictability](../common/long-lead-enso-predictability.md) on the **physical [recharge oscillator / XRO](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md)** route: an [extended nonlinear recharge oscillator (XRO)](xro.md) couples core ENSO recharge–discharge dynamics to seasonally modulated interactions with other global ocean modes, yielding explainable multi-season forecasts. [XRO development · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

Keep Library ENSO forecasting routes distinct:

1. **Physical recharge oscillators / XRO (this paper)** — low-order [XRO](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md) that extends a nonlinear RO with AR representations of NPMM/SPMM, IOB/IOD/SIOD, and TNA/ATL3/SASD; skill gains are attributed mainly to remote-mode initial-condition memory. [XRO · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [XRO = nRO + modes · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [memory of other modes · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)
2. **Deep learning / AI** — long-lead neural forecasts (e.g. Ham et al.; 3D-Geoformer) can reach ~18–24 months but do not yet map skill to specific physical processes; XRO is positioned as comparable in skill and more explainable. [AI skill vs explainability · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)
3. **Climate correlation networks** and **physics-guided hybrids** — not implemented here; see Library neighbors [network/SysSampEn](../paper-f2e5cb4961564e52/index.md), [DESN](../paper-a56c3ee1b33d45b2/index.md), and [Dynamical-DL](../paper-eee57a8421b14218/index.md). The RO survey [Vialard et al. 2025](../paper-e95322ea3e1f4a2a/index.md) synthesizes RO→XRO context.

## Key method

[XRO](xro.md) is fitted primarily on [ORAS5](../common/oras5.md) (1979–2022) and multi-product SST/WWV indices; skill is compared with a tropical-Pacific-only nRO, IRI ensembles, [NMME](../common/nmme.md) dynamical models, and AI Niño3.4 forecasts. [ORAS5 stochastic sim · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [OOS vs nRO/IRI/AI · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [control vs NMME · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [control setup · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

Uninitialized / decoupled / relaxation sensitivity experiments isolate ExPO, Indian Ocean, and Atlantic contributions; uninitialized runs are preferred for nearly additive basin attribution. [three frameworks · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [uninitialized preferred · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

CMIP5/6-trained XRO operators (91 historical runs) diagnose how biases in ENSO dynamics and mode coupling reduce forecast skill. [CMIP-trained XRO' · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [bias correction · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

## Key results

- **Skill:** Out-of-sample and control Niño3.4 correlation remains skilful to about **16–18 months**, with control ACC still above **0.5** at 18 months—systematically above individual/mean [NMME](../common/nmme.md) dynamical models and comparable to the most skilful AI models; the spring predictability barrier is much weaker than in nRO. [Abstract 16–18 mo · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [ACC>0.5 @18 mo · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [weaker SPB · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Fig. 2 summary · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)
- **Sources:** Skill enhancement vs nRO comes primarily from initial-condition memory of non-ENSO modes (ExPO/IO/AO), with strong seasonality (e.g. NPMM-dominated ExPO; IOD-dominated IO; TNA/SASD in AO). [memory · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [basin seasonality · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Fig. 3 summary · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)
- **Model biases:** Correcting ENSO internal dynamics and remote feedbacks onto ENSO in CMIP-fitted operators improves Niño3.4 skill; XRO2 (Niño3+Niño4) further targets ENSO spatial types and pantropical SSTA. [bias corrections · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Fig. 5 · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [XRO2 types · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

## Limits

Deterministic skill is emphasized (stochastic ensembles deferred); multiplicative state-dependent noise is acknowledged but not fully constrained by record length; pantropical regression skill is weaker in the Caribbean; further multi-timescale (MJO/WWB) and decadal extensions are proposed, not demonstrated. [deterministic focus · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [multiplicative noise · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Caribbean · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6) [Discussion extensions · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07534-6)

# The El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) Recharge Oscillator Conceptual Model: Achievements and Future Prospects

**Review article.** *Reviews of Geophysics* **63**, e2024RG000843 (2025). DOI [10.1029/2024RG000843](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843). [REVIEW ARTICLE · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Citation · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)

## Survey scope and research questions

This CLIVAR-linked synthesis surveys the [recharge oscillator (RO)](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md) as a low-dimensional conceptual model of [ENSO](../common/enso.md), asking how well RO frameworks encapsulate ENSO mechanisms, reproduce observed and CMIP properties, and can be extended to pattern diversity, remote-basin influences, and climate-change questions. [Abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Purpose · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Focus on the RO · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)

## Taxonomy (this survey’s framework)

Survey synthesis distinguishes complexity levels of the same RO family (not separate Library forecasting routes):

1. **Linear RO (LRO)** — two ODEs for equatorial SST \(T\) and heat content \(h\), with Bjerknes feedback \(R\) and delayed oceanic recharge/discharge. [LRO Eqs. 1–2 · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [RO recipe · p. 27](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
2. **Stochastic RO (SRO)** — adds noise (mainly WWBs) because fitted annual-mean growth is damped. [SRO · p. 14](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [stable + noise · p. 16](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
3. **Nonlinear RO (NRO)** — multiplicative noise and quadratic/cubic terms for asymmetry and extremes; seasonal \(R(t)\) for phase locking and the spring barrier. [NRO · p. 14](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [seasonality · p. 19](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [spring barrier · p. 20](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
4. **Extensions beyond the tropical Pacific** — multi-SST RO variants for EP/CP diversity; [XRO](../common/extended-recharge-oscillator.md) coupling of an NRO to remote climate modes (as reviewed from Zhao et al. 2024; Library `paper-e09bd415cb6849f6`, hub not yet built). [diversity Key Point · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Fig. 14 XRO · p. 25](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [XRO skill · p. 26](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)

Keep this **physical conceptual-model** route distinct from Library [deep learning](../common/deep-learning.md), [climate correlation networks](../common/climate-correlation-networks.md), and [physics-guided hybrids](../common/physics-guided-hybrid-enso-forecasting.md) (e.g. [DESN](../paper-a56c3ee1b33d45b2/index.md), [CTEFNet](../paper-db78aff21cda4d55/index.md), [Dynamical-DL](../paper-eee57a8421b14218/index.md)).

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

The Introduction places ENSO in tropical Pacific ocean–atmosphere coupling, then reviews conceptual oscillators (delayed, advective-reflective, western Pacific, unified) before concentrating on the RO as the leading simple unifying framework that explicitly carries heat-content memory and can be fitted to observations and models. [Why ENSO matters · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [conceptual models · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Focus on the RO · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)

## What the survey reports RO can explain

As synthesized here (survey judgment grounded in the authors’ ORAS5/CMIP6 RO fits and literature):

- **Amplitude** — NRO fits recover observed and CMIP6 ENSO amplitude (reported \(r = 0.97\)); stability and noise dominate near observed parameters. [amplitude · p. 16](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Fig. 8 · p. 16](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
- **Seasonality & spring barrier** — seasonal \(R(t)\) reproduces boreal-winter peaking and the spring predictability barrier. [seasonality · p. 20](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [spring barrier · p. 20](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Fig. 10 · p. 18](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
- **Dominant timescale** — BWJ/Wyrtki period tracks CMIP6 periodicity (reported \(R = 0.87\)) but underestimates absolute period (~3 vs ~4.2 years in observations, per survey). [Wyrtki index · p. 21](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
- **Asymmetry** — SRO is nearly symmetric; NRO multiplicative/quadratic nonlinearities recover stronger El Niño than La Niña (survey notes sources of nonlinearity remain ambiguous). [Fig. 12 · p. 19](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [ambiguous nonlinearities · p. 22](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)

## Pressing topics and open questions (survey synthesis)

1. **Pattern diversity** — warm-pool geometric RO vs 3–6 variable extensions; minimal physics still unsettled. [minimal RO for diversity · p. 23](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [synthesis diversity · p. 28](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
2. **Remote basins / XRO** — Indian Ocean, NPMM, and tropical Atlantic contribute differently to dynamics vs predictability; XRO hindcasts (Zhao et al. 2024, as reported here) quantify long-lead skill gains. [RO perspective · p. 25](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [Fig. 14 · p. 25](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
3. **Warmer world** — CMIP points to stronger future ENSO extremes, but mean-state trends and RO/BWJ diagnostics do not yet yield a consensus mechanism. [RO and climate change · p. 29](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [RO status · p. 27](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)
4. **Way forward** — nine questions on RO parameters, choice of \(h\), diversity/extremes, forecasts, inter-basin links, multidecadal variability, mean-state theory, DL cross-breeding, and climate change; plus a planned community RO code release. [§7 · p. 29](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [DL cross-breeding · p. 30](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843) [community RO · p. 31](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024RG000843)

## Limits of this wiki projection

Survey secondary source: representative numerical claims are attributed as this review reports them. Do not treat survey RO–CMIP correlations as original experiments, or rank them against Library DL/hybrid ACC curves under unequal setups. XRO primary paper remains `paper-e09bd415cb6849f6` (no hub yet).

# Combined dynamical-deep learning ENSO forecasts

*Nature Communications* **16**, 3845 (2025). DOI [10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8). [DOI · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [Published 24 Apr 2025 · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)

## Problem and idea

[ENSO](../common/enso.md) forecasting has long relied on dynamical models and statistical/ML approaches, with the spring predictability barrier (SPB) remaining a central difficulty. [Introduction · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) Recent [deep learning](../common/deep-learning.md) models trained on large climate-model archives often beat **individual** dynamical models, yet how to combine DL and dynamical strengths is still open. [DL vs dynamical · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [Abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)

This paper addresses [long-lead ENSO predictability](../common/long-lead-enso-predictability.md) on the **[hybrid dynamical–DL](../common/physics-guided-hybrid-enso-forecasting.md)** route: after showing CNN and 3D-Geoformer skill matches the NMME **dynamic-model mean**, it proposes a combined Dynamical-DL Forecast with two strategies that outperform either family alone. [Dynamical-DL · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [DL ≈ model mean · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

Keep Library ENSO routes distinct:

1. **Hybrid dynamical–DL (this paper)** — fuse multi-model dynamical forecasts with CMIP6-trained DL (CNN, 3D-Geoformer) via averaging (Strategy 1) or DL-guided ensemble subsampling (Strategy 2). [Strategy 1 · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [Strategy 2 · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)
2. **Deep learning** — field-based neural ENSO models that can exceed most single dynamical members; here reproduced and then combined, not treated as a complete substitute. [DL route · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [vs NMME · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)
3. **Physical recharge oscillators / XRO** — cited as evidence that dynamical knowledge plus statistical algorithms matter (Zhao et al. 2024; Library `paper-e09bd415cb6849f6`, hub not yet built); this paper does **not** implement XRO. [XRO citation · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [Ref. 33 · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)
4. **Climate correlation networks** — not used here.

Library neighbors with hubs: [physics-guided DESN](../paper-a56c3ee1b33d45b2/index.md) (XRO-mode hybrid); [CTEFNet](../paper-db78aff21cda4d55/index.md) (DL). Do not rank skill across unequal setups.

## Key method

[Combined Dynamical-DL Forecast](dynamical-dl-forecast.md) reproduces Ham et al. CNN and Zhou & Zhang 3D-Geoformer trained on [CMIP6](../common/cmip6.md) historical SST/SSH (31 models), validates against [ORAS5](../common/oras5.md) (1982–2018), and compares to eight [NMME](../common/nmme.md) coupled hindcasts (≤1-year lead). [ORAS5/CMIP6 · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [NMME · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [CNN · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [3D-Geoformer · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)

- **Strategy 1:** equal-weight average of NMME dynamic-model mean + CNN + 3D-Geoformer. [Strategy 1 methods · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)
- **Strategy 2:** use DL Niño3.4 as a “First-Guess” to keep the closest 50% of a dynamical model’s ensemble members. [Strategy 2 methods · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)

## Key results

- **DL vs dynamical mean:** Year-round Niño3.4 ACC of CNN/3D-Geoformer stays useful (ACC ≥ 0.5) to about **16–18** months and matches the NMME dynamic-model mean for year-round and March-initialized (SPB-crossing) forecasts, while beating most individual NMME members. [Fig. 1 / ACC · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)
- **Strategy 1:** ACC rises significantly beyond either DL model or the dynamical multi-model mean for most year-round leads (except ~7–8 months) and for SPB forecasts beyond 4 months; significant ACC gains in 35.6% / 51.5% / 50.8% of 132 month–lead targets vs 3D-Geoformer / CNN / dynamical mean. [Strategy 1 skill · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)
- **Strategy 2:** For 5 of 8 NMME models, DL-guided sub-ensembles beat that model’s full-ensemble mean (notably beyond ~8 months); e.g. COLA-RSMAS-CCSM4 ACC rises from **0.67 to 0.77** near 9-month lead with CNN selection. [Strategy 2 · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [0.67→0.77 · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)

## Limits

Dynamical leads (hence Strategy 1) stop at ~1 year; DL systematically underestimates ENSO peak intensity; real-time use is constrained by reanalysis latency (e.g. ORAS5 ~half-month lag). [1-year limit · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [peak bias · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8) [ORAS5 latency · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59173-8)

Paper-specific application of the [climate network / complexity](../common/climate-correlation-networks.md) early-warning suite to the **2026** [ENSO](../common/enso.md) outlook.

# Climate network and complexity based ENSO forecast for 2026

**Preprint.** arXiv:2602.14773v1 [physics.ao-ph] (16 Feb 2026). [arXiv header · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)

## Problem and idea

[ENSO](../common/enso.md) drives interannual climate variability, yet operational dynamical and statistical forecasts often struggle with the spring predictability barrier and short reliable leads. [ENSO phases · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [SPB / ~6 months · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)

This paper issues a **2026** outlook on the [climate correlation networks](../common/climate-correlation-networks.md) / complexity route: it applies previously published climate-network and System Sample Entropy (SysSampEn) early-warning methods (plus El Niño type and La Niña–neutral predictors) rather than a new DL, XRO, or dynamical–DL hybrid model. [Abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [two methods · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [2026 forecasts · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

Keep Library ENSO routes distinct:

1. **Climate correlation networks / complexity (this paper)** — cooperative teleconnection links and Niño3.4 complexity (SysSampEn) as ~1-year-ahead El Niño onset/magnitude precursors. [network + SysSampEn · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [cooperativity · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
2. **Dynamical GCMs vs statistical models** — Introduction framing of the broader forecasting landscape and the spring barrier that motivates early-warning alternatives. [GCM vs statistical · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [operational limits · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
3. **Deep learning, XRO, and physics-guided hybrids** — present elsewhere in this Library ([CTEFNet](../paper-db78aff21cda4d55/index.md), [DESN](../paper-a56c3ee1b33d45b2/index.md), [Dynamical-DL](../paper-eee57a8421b14218/index.md)); this preprint does **not** implement those routes. Zhao et al. 2024 XRO (`paper-e09bd415cb6849f6`) appears only among bibliographic ENSO models, not as this paper's method.

## Key method

[Climate network + SysSampEn forecasting](climate-network-syssampen.md) combines:

- **Climate network (primarily [NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1](../common/ncep-ncar-reanalysis-1.md) SAT):** mean link strength S(t) vs learned threshold; restrictive version (ii) requires ONI to stay below 0.5°C after the alarm. [S(t) precursor · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [alarm rule · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [NCEP data · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
- **SysSampEn (primarily [ERA5](../common/era5.md) near-surface temperature):** complexity in Niño3.4 mapped by linear regression to El Niño magnitude and onset. [SysSampEn · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [ERA5 input · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [2026 SysSampEn · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
- **Type and phase refinements:** western–central Pacific SST difference for EP vs CP type; interannual ONI logistic regression for La Niña vs neutral when El Niño is absent. [type index · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [La Niña vs neutral · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)

An ERA5-based network sensitivity test shows a partial threshold crossing by end-2025, illustrating reanalysis dependence. [ERA5 network · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [partial alarm · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)

## Key results

- **Diverging 2026 signals:** NCEP network version (ii) forecasts **absence** of El Niño with ~**91.4%** skill for absence forecasts; SysSampEn forecasts onset with **71.4%** and magnitude **0.84±0.36°C**. [91.4% absence · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [71.4% / 0.84°C · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [divergence · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
- **Combined outlook:** Laplace succession on past mismatches yields **37.5%** El Niño onset; given no El Niño, logistic ONI implies ~**70.9%** neutral vs ~**29.1%** La Niña, hence unconditional **44.3%** neutral / **18.2%** La Niña for NDJ 2026/27. [37.5% · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [44.3% / 18.2% · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [Fig. 6 summary · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
- **Vs NOAA CPC:** Combined El Niño probability is **lower** than the January 2026 CPC plume (**61%** El Niño for ASO 2026). [vs CPC 61% · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [Fig. 6 · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
- **If El Niño:** EP type with **76.9%** probability. [EP 76.9% · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)
- **Network skill context:** Real-time network forecasts 2012–2025 are mostly correct; authors note the network precursor skill is strong on reanalyses but absent/low in [CMIP6](../common/cmip6.md)/CMIP5 runs. [real-time skill · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773) [CMIP skill gap · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2602.14773)

## Limits

Preprint status; 2026 outcomes are forecasts, not verified events; network vs SysSampEn disagreement depends partly on NCEP vs ERA5; EP-type vs weak SysSampEn magnitude is only partly reconciled; do not rank this outlook against Library DL/hybrid ACC curves under unequal setups.
